title: Security questionnaire desk
_comment: Answer vendor security questionnaires from house knowledge. Batch fans out questions; never invent controls that are not in knowledge.

answer_question.description: Answer one questionnaire item from mounted knowledge. If knowledge is silent, mark needs_human and do not guess.

input_schema._comment: ONE item, answered from mounted knowledge. The description is explicit that silence means needs_human and never a guess — which is only possible if there is a question to be silent about.

question.description: The questionnaire item, verbatim as the buyer wrote it. REQUIRED.

question_id.description: The buyer's own reference for it, so the answer lands in the right row of their form.

fill_questionnaire.description: Parse the questionnaire into items, fan out answer_question children, then compile a review packet from the batch.

needs.description: What this run needs from the CLIENT before it can produce the work, in the client’s own words — one plain item per entry. Name the thing THEY would name: the document, the answer, the decision, the access. Populate this WHENEVER the run cannot finish because something only the client has is missing. Each entry becomes a request in their portal with an upload box; what they send is mounted into the next run’s ./inputs/, so an accurate ask here is what unblocks the work. Never use our nouns — a request naming a case, a schema or a connection id is unanswerable by the person receiving it. At most four, most important first. Leave absent when the work completed — an empty ask sent to a client is worse than silence.

artifacts.description:
THE WORK ITSELF, not a description of it.

Every deliverable task in this system produced a summary and nothing else, and a client scored one 3/10 partly for that reason: they were sent an account of work rather than the work. A service business does not sell reports about bookkeeping, it sells reconciled books; it does not sell a note about a questionnaire, it sells the questionnaire answered.

So this carries the artifact. A file you wrote to ./output/ and its name, or a URL to something live, or a repository. The `client_summary` is the covering note that goes WITH this — it is not a substitute for it, and a deliverable with an empty `artifacts` array is a deliverable that did not deliver.

Say so plainly in the summary if you genuinely could not produce the artifact, and why. That is a real outcome. Pretending the summary is the work is not.

For this job: THE FILLED QUESTIONNAIRE, in the format it arrived in. This is the whole job: the client sends a spreadsheet of 46 questions and buys it back answered. A summary of having answered it is not the deliverable and cannot be submitted to anybody.

kind.description: `file` for something you wrote to ./output/, `url` for something live, `repo` for source.

name.description: What it is, in the client's words. 'September ledger', not 'output.csv'.

path.description: Relative to ./output/ for a file. Required for kind=file.

what_it_is.description: One line the client reads before opening it.

sections.heading: Where this questionnaire stands
sections.must: How many items are answered, how many need a person, and whether it can be returned as it is.

sections.heading: Answers
sections.must: Every item with its answer and the control or document it rests on. An answer with no source is the thing this trade must never send.

sections.heading: Needs a human
sections.must: Each item nobody could answer from the evidence, and what would be needed to answer it. Never fill these in to make the packet look complete.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.must: Who has to sign off, what is blocking return, and the date the requester expects it.

input_schema._comment: PER-PACKET. Parses one questionnaire, fans out a child per item, compiles the packet. The blueprint deliberately does NOT schedule this — its own note says scheduling it empty would burn a run with nothing to parse — so requiring the packet here makes that reasoning enforceable rather than a comment.

questionnaire.description: The packet to answer — its text, or the artifact id it arrived as. REQUIRED.

buyer.description: Who is asking. Changes what may be said and how much.

desk_run.description: The morning sweep across open questionnaires: which packet has no draft, which is waiting on a human, which is ready to send after you approve.

summary.description: What a desk lead needs this morning. If there are no packets, say so — do not invent a vendor.

input_schema._comment: THE MORNING SWEEP over open questionnaires. Takes nothing: which packet needs what is a fact about stored rows, and `fill_questionnaire` is the per-packet job that DOES require its packet.

intake.ask: Which controls do you actually have, in your words — not a vendor's checklist?
intake.why: Every answer is drafted from this. Silence here is answered needs-a-human, never invented.
intake.example: SSO via Google Workspace, laptops encrypted with FileVault, customer data in RDS in eu-west-2, backups daily to a second region. No SOC 2 yet — we say so.

intake.ask: Where does the evidence live, and what must a human still attach?
intake.why: Stops a draft that cites a policy nobody can produce when the vendor asks.
intake.example: Policies in Drive/Security. Pen-test PDF is last year's — flag it. I attach insurance certificates myself.

intake.ask: When must it stop and come to you rather than answering?
intake.why: Attesting to a control you do not have is the expensive error. Draw the line.
intake.example: Anything about breach history I have not written down. Any 'we encrypt at rest' that is not in controls. Anything that goes to a customer as a signed attestation.

client_connections.ask: Connect the Drive folder with your evidence pack
client_connections.detail: Policies, SOC reports, and prior questionnaire answers.

intake_asks.ask: The blank questionnaire you need filled

workflows.name: workbook
workflows.description: Turn a grid you have already decided is correct into a real Excel workbook (.xlsx), attached to this delivery automatically. Use it for anything a client will sort, filter or forward — a longlist, a ranking table, a budget, a control matrix. Do NOT use it to do arithmetic: it formats what you give it and never re-totals a column.

currency.description: ISO-4217. Omit it and money renders as a plain number, which is honest.

tabs.description: One per sheet. A tab per schedule beats one sheet with blank rows between sections.

note.description: A caveat rendered above the header, for something that must be read before the numbers.

rows.description: Each row is an array of cells. A plain string or number is fine; for a formatted number use {kind:"n", v:1234, format:"money"|"pct"|"int"} and for a date {kind:"d", v:"2026-04-30"}.
